3.speaker: Player
3.text: “I was young and I made a mistake.”

5.speaker: Deivid Wisci
5.text: “I will start by providing a brief overview of our current status with our neighbours. What would you like to start with?”

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “I want to know more about Valgsland.”

23.speaker: Deivid Wisci
23.text: “Our *brotherly* nation to our north-east, Agnolia. They are still diplomatically non-aligned and probably has one of the most democratic systems between our neighbours.”

24.speaker: Deivid Wisci
24.text: “Our cousins of old across the Markian Sea wish to have good relations with us. As we all know, Valgsland is a socialist republic aligned with United Contana. They are an important regional player.”

25.speaker: Deivid Wisci
25.text: “It is tumultuous in the south, as always. Wiktor Smolak is expanding his powers among protests from Wehzek people. However, he is quite positive about a normalisation of relationship between our countries.”

26.speaker: Deivid Wisci
26.text: “Additionally, the latest numbers indicate that currently, a million Agno-Sordish citizens live in the Agnland region of Sordland.”

27.speaker: Iosef Lancea
27.text: “They haven't been in good standing with us for the past two hundred years. Recently, they have also joined the Communist Contanan Security Pact, subjugating themselves to United Contana.”

28.speaker: Deivid Wisci
28.text: “Our main goal should be to avoid a refugee crisis like the late 1920’s. That civil war had major security and economic repercussions on Sordish soil.”

29.speaker: Iosef Lancea
29.text: “In addition, a relaxed immigration policy was one of Agnolia's main requests. Which is unacceptable. Most of the migrants in our country haven't even assimilated into Sordish culture. Adding more won't help.”

30.speaker: Lucian Galade
30.text: “Unfortunately, billions of Sordish Ren worth of cargo is transported close to Valgslandian maritime borders on the Markian Sea and the Grey Strait.”

31.speaker: Deivid Wisci
31.text: “Two important neighbouring countries remain. Lespia and Rumburg. Which would you like to hear about first?”

39.speaker: Deivid Wisci
39.text: “Our southern neighbour is aligning itself more and more with Arcasia. Lespia is currently led by Prime Minister Patricio Alvarez.”

40.speaker: Iosef Lancea
40.text: “You paid the price for your mistake so it doesn't matter anymore.”

41.speaker: Deivid Wisci
41.text: “Now to the most troublesome nation; Rumburg. A constitutional monarchy led by Queen Beatrice Livingston.”

44.speaker: Lucian Galade
44.text: “There are hundreds of very privileged oligarchs who invest inside and outside of Lespia. Some made significant business investments in the cities of Benfi and Valgen.”

45.speaker: Deivid Wisci
45.text: “I am certain that the recession has a lot to do with their retraction of investments. Once they see that money isn't in the picture they vanish rather quickly because they are capitalists.”

46.speaker: Lucian Galade
46.text: “We could use their aggressive attitude against them by convincing the international community.”

47.speaker: Iosef Lancea
47.text: “While Thornbourgh openly denies such claims, their past and current actions make it clear that they want to destabilize us.”

51.speaker: Deivid Wisci
51.text: “This covers the overview of the current situation. We will move on to our trade choice and the response to Rumburg's diplomatic escalation.”

52.speaker: Deivid Wisci
52.text: “Our past relations have been great but during the last decade, their investments to Sordland dwindled due to our instability.”

56.speaker: Deivid Wisci
56.text: “Unsurprisingly, the Agnolian Prime Minister Maartin Van Hoorten is expecting better cooperation through a new, fairer trade deal with us. It was one of his election mandates.”

57.speaker: Player
57.text: “We'll think about his request. The matter is still on the table.”

58.speaker: Player
58.text: “A more comprehensive trade deal sounds beneficial to all sides.”

59.speaker: Deivid Wisci
59.text: “Recently, the relationship has warmed up thanks to Emmerich Hegel. As a result, diplomatic talks can be conducted in the future."

60.speaker: Player
60.text: “It's not easy to forget about the Great Fire of Conriat. Thousands of lives were lost that day.”

61.speaker: Player
61.text: “Breaking the ice with Valgsland could be good, if we are to rise diplomatically.”

63.speaker: Lucian Galade
63.text: “This causes significant risks to our imports and exports in the case of a deterioration in relations.”

64.speaker: Deivid Wisci
64.text: “But if we want to help them, we must not treat refugees like we did in the '30s. I still can’t stomach the inhumanity those people suffered.”

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “A trade agreement with them would improve stability and increase mutual trade.”

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “Why help such a disorganized state? Not sure about what we can do to help them.”

67.speaker: Deivid Wisci
67.text: “They are strong and have the motivation, as well as the means, to damage us. We shouldn't give them any reasons to pursue aggression.”

68.speaker: Player
68.text: “I will take your advice in consideration.”

69.speaker: Player
69.text: “Rumburg is and always will be a rogue like state. Nothing can be done about them.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “Lespia is a sleeping giant. We should not awake them.”

71.speaker: Player
71.text: “They keep turning a blind eye towards the region. Thinking that Lespia is above it all.”

72.speaker: Iosef Lancea
72.text: “They have shown a selfish attitude during the Wehlen Civil War by closing their borders and funnelling refugees to cross into Sordland.”

76.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
76.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_FPnT_Listened_Hub_Agnolia"] == true   or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_FPnT_Listened_Hub_Valgsland"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_FPnT_Listened_Hub_Wehlen"] == true) == false

77.speaker: Iosef Lancea
77.text: “The weapons caches found by our intelligence agency clearly shows what their goals are. Our military must be steadfast and our diplomacy valiant.”

78.speaker: Deivid Wisci
78.text: “It is in our national interest to prevent the formation of a failed state on our western border.”

79.speaker: Lucian Galade
79.text: “They are the jewel of the continent and the second largest economy in Eastern Merkopa. Though wealthy, Lespia suffers from excessive economic inequality.”

80.speaker: Iosef Lancea
80.text: “I highly advise caution and calculated action against Rumburg. Our military must be prepared, the threat is real.”

82.speaker: Iosef Lancea
82.text: “Soldiers do not decide on what is right. Soldiers do what they are told to do.”

83.speaker: Iosef Lancea
83.text: “We are actively monitoring the sea routes and cargo ships. For now, there is no immediate threat. But we don't know what can happen in the future.”

84.speaker: Lucian Galade
84.text: “Wehlen has been increasingly aligning itself towards the communist alliance, another point to analyse.”

85.speaker: Deivid Wisci
85.text: “Our focus should be on the current matters. The Bludish minority is very large inside Wehlen too, which is a factor to consider.”

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: He opened his mouth to say something but Deivid cut in.

87.speaker: Deivid Wisci
87.text: “They surely are a powerful nation. Despite that, they don't tend to meddle in the region and haven't for a long time, with the exception of Wehlen. Let's not antagonize them.”

88.speaker: Deivid Wisci
88.text: “The Lespian mentality is influenced by a certain aura of heroism and specialism. Their moral compass is different from ours.”

89.speaker: Deivid Wisci
89.text: “These types of nations will always try to make up a casus belli, a reason to declare war.”

90.speaker: Deivid Wisci
90.text: “We can act in our limits and make sure we are prepared for anything. Sword rattling is not advised in my opinion.”

91.speaker: Deivid Wisci
91.text: “They have shown similar behaviour to their neighbouring countries before but we must be cautious.”

92.speaker: Player
92.text: “We must prevent them from interfering in our affairs.”

93.speaker: Deivid Wisci
93.text: “It could be but it would also mean that we would draw closer to the Arcasia block and near the Arcasian Treaty Organisation.”

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “Allying with the richest regional nation could be beneficial.”

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: Iosef looked stern and full of resolve.

96.speaker: Deivid Wisci
96.text: “We are always in dialogue with our Rumburg ambassador to make sure a channel is open to solve disputes.”

97.speaker: Player
97.text: “The Rumburg threat is one of our top priorities. You can be assured of that.”

98.speaker: Lucian Galade
98.text: “Either way, treading carefully with them would be the safest bet.”

99.speaker: Deivid Wisci
99.text: “I agree, some in our government are taking the issue out of proportion.”

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “I think the threat is far too overblown.”

101.speaker: Deivid Wisci
101.text: “I completely agree. Lespia has for a long time benefited from us through our old tariffs. They are after exploitation.”

102.speaker: Player
102.text: “Our values are too different with Lespia. It will be hard to see eye to eye.”

103.speaker: Deivid Wisci
103.text: “Everything comes at a cost. In Lespia the cost is wealth inequality but business people are getting richer and richer.”

104.speaker: Player
104.text: “The Capitalism of Lespia is inspirational to me. Look at their economic power.”

105.speaker: Lucian Galade
105.text: “Their abrupt announcement about the closure of the Rumburg consulate in Lachaven is yet another step in their escalation.”

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: Lucian grabbed the Lachaven Times newspaper and put his finger on the article about the latest diplomatic incident.

108.speaker: Iosef Lancea
108.text: “In fact, there had been a similar refugee situation in the past. Even Mr. President himself chose to disobey direct orders from his commanding officer at the time.”

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: He was right, I did remember that winter. I remembered the despair in the refugees' eyes when we forcefully escorted them back to the Wehlen border.

111.speaker: Player
111.text: “And you made me sleep in a prison cell for it. I will never forget that.”

112.speaker: Narrator
112.text: He opened his mouth to continue but Deivid cut in.

113.speaker: Iosef Lancea
113.text: “That is the point of disciplinary action.”

114.speaker: Lucian Galade
114.text: “Which creates a link between foreign policy and our internal affairs. These people have suffered socio-economically, which led them to crime and other problems.”

115.speaker: Lucian Galade
115.text: “Economic stagnation is a worry for them. Their primary issue is their heavy reliance on foreign investment from us.”

116.speaker: Deivid Wisci
116.text: “It's also the most significant sea power in almost all of Merkopa. It is the only country that can rival the superpowers with their navy. We had hostile relations with them after several wars in the 19th century, which we wouldn't want to experience again.”

117.speaker: Deivid Wisci
117.text: “Despite purging the Wehzek communists, reports indicate that they have been warming up to Contanan international aid. As you know, Wehlen’s stability was always a concern for the region.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “We should maintain the existing agreement. We can't lose our advantage.”

119.speaker: Deivid Wisci
119.text: “We could secure them as allies if we make concessions in a new agreement. Rumburg is our common threat.”

123.speaker: Iosef Lancea
123.text: “On top of that, territorial issues have been flaring up between Agnolia and Valgsland because of the Heljiland Island. The Sordish Navy is very concerned with this volatile situation.”

124.speaker: Deivid Wisci
124.text: “Both sides could gain from it but Agnolia has more to win than us. They want to protect their weaker industries which we are profiting from selling our goods to.”

125.speaker: Deivid Wisci
125.text: “That would be the most pragmatic choice. Our export tariffs to Agnolia are incredibly low under the current agreement.”

126.speaker: Deivid Wisci
126.text: “Holding grudges about the past wouldn't be a logical strategy if we are focusing on pragmatic foreign policy.”

127.speaker: Deivid Wisci
127.text: “There would be many bargaining chips discussed, but Wehlen could be a new partner in the region. We would also invest in stability there.”

128.speaker: Iosef Lancea
128.text: “You should be. We have already witnessed several society shifting waves of migration.”

129.speaker: Iosef Lancea
129.text: “I would re-think the matter seriously because it has great influence on our society and values.”

132.speaker: Deivid Wisci
132.text: “And when we had our civil war, they were there for us. That is how refugee rights work internationally.”

133.speaker: Player
133.text: “Sordland paid enough by housing millions of refugees during the Wehlen Civil War. No more.”

134.speaker: Deivid Wisci
134.text: “It does pose many risks, but we could ensure that we have more influence in the region by increasing our trade and border security.”

135.speaker: Player
135.text: “We shouldn't take any sides between the regional powers.”

136.speaker: Deivid Wisci
136.text: “I agree they could be potential allies in my opinion. The situation in the region necessitates that we find allies.”

137.speaker: Player
137.text: “The strait is of high strategic value to us.”

138.speaker: Deivid Wisci
138.text: “It could lead us to be squeezed between the two with no protection. It's a potential situation to be considered.”

140.speaker: Lucian Galade
140.text: “Iosef, the Navy is keeping an eye on the situation from a distance, right?”

141.speaker: Lucian Galade
141.text: “We should remember that we promised to tighten our immigration laws in the election campaign.”

144.speaker: Lucian Galade
144.text: “We should remember that we promised to keep our immigration laws relaxed in the election campaign.”

145.speaker: Deivid Wisci
145.text: “Agnolia is our most friendly neighbour. We have been allies for the longest time after Rumburg's actions in the region. This fact needs to be a part of the equation.”

146.speaker: Iosef Lancea
146.text: “One of the demands of President Smolak was to tighten our immigration laws, so the political refugees don't escape to Sordland. There has been a recent purge that pushed many Bludish to flee to Bergia. It is definitely troubling.”

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: He was right, I did remember that winter. I remembered how cold it was when I let the refugees slip through. I was discharged of my duties as a result, by Major Iosef Lancea, no less, spending the rest of my service cleaning toilets and sleeping in a cell.

151.speaker: Iosef Lancea
151.text: “Gumren Outpost has regained its importance due to this. I'm sure you would remember that winter at the border outpost, Mr. President...”
